_source: C1 finalized from speller close-up photo (2026-07-17): tile rows are the 24 lowercase letters, then final sigma + 3 single accents + 2 breathings + 1 combo, then 5 more breathing+accent combos + the 3 iota-subscript composites. Inventory = 25 letters + 11 marks + 3 composites (39 tiles). All six breathing+accent combinations exist (incl. rough+grave and smooth+grave). On-screen arrangement is the app's own; this inventory is the contract. Diacritic 'apply' = combining sequence appended to the previous character, then NFC-normalize.
_extension_5d: 5D Phase 0 (divergence log D-15, layout A chosen by Nathanael): one added bottom row of punctuation keys + a space bar. The original on-screen keyboard has neither, and the chapter-3 Scripture Memory Spelling Exercise types a 14-word verse; chapter 6's Spell Greek Phrase needs the space too. Punctuation covers the Scripture Memory family through chapter 8 (comma, raised dot, period) plus the Greek question mark. NO CAPITALS and no shift layer: the checking policy folds case under both 'With Accents' settings instead. The question-mark tile inserts U+003B, which is what U+037E normalizes to under NFC. This file is the SHARED contract for every spell surface app-wide; SpellActivity reads it in preference to any inline activity.spellerTiles copy so a chapter cannot fork the keyboard.
_extension_5e3: APOSTROPHE tile added (divergence log D-29, Nathanael 2026-08-07). Chapter 2 TEACHES elision by name -- Learn Marks has an 'Apostrophe' topic deriving dia + autou -> di' autou, the Marking Recognition Drill scores 'Apostrophe' as an answer distinct from 'Smooth Breathing' and 'Coronis', and the Quick Review marks chart lists 'Apostrophe: ( U+1FBD ) elided letters'. Chapter 4's Scripture Memory Spelling Exercise then requires the learner to type di' in John 14:6b, and until now no tile could produce it. The original has no apostrophe key either and represents the elision mark as a smooth breathing ON the iota -- it accepts that form and rejects a real apostrophe -- but that is the original working around its own missing key, not Greek: the elision mark is a spacing apostrophe (U+1FBD GREEK KORONIS) and a breathing can only sit on a word-initial vowel or rho. The tile inserts U+0027 and the delivered data now stores U+0027 (2026-08-07): the koronis is a smooth breathing drawn over nothing, which is what the original used because it had no apostrophe key, and it is wrong for Greek. The checker accepts the apostrophe, any of its Unicode spellings, the original's smooth-breathing form, and nothing at all (D-18 punctuation optional), so no learner is punished for typing it the way the original taught them. The key is PRINTED and INSERTS U+0027, the straight vertical typewriter apostrophe. U+1FBD is the same comma-above shape as the smooth-breathing key one row above it, and the two were indistinguishable on device (Nathanael, 2026-08-07) -- which is the same confusion that made the original conflate them in the first place. U+0027 is the only apostrophe form with no curl, so it cannot be mistaken for the breathing, the acute or the grave. The mark is REQUIRED where a verse elides: omitting it is now a misspelling, unlike other punctuation (D-18), because an elision mark carries meaning.
